 Judgment

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Bidar (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.296/2019 vide its judgment and award dated 17.12.2020.

2. The claimants contend that they are the dependant legal heirs of deceased - Tribhuvan Singh, who died in a road traffic accident on 12.04.2019 when the motorcycle ridden by him bearing registration No.KA-38/L-3310 was rear ended by another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-38/H-8186 (henceforth referred to as 'offending motorcycle').
As a result, the deceased fell on the road and suffered serious head injuries and fell unconscious.
Though he was shifted in ambulance, where he was administered first-aid and was shifted to NC: 2023:KHC-K:5563 Government Hospital, Bidar and referred to Hyderabad.
Later, he was shifted to Omni Hospital, Hyderabad, where he was admitted as an inpatient and however, he did not respond to the treatment.
He was thereafter shifted to Max Cure Hospital, Hyderabad but he died on 13.04.2019.

The claimants contended that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month as a Supervisor in the factory run by his father under the name and style "M/s. D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers"
which was Super Grade Electrical Contractor.

entities.text: M/s. D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: They therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending motorcycle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer of the offending vehicle who denied the accident as well as the death of Tribhuvan Singh in the accident.
It denied any negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
It also denied the avocation of the deceased and the dependency of the claimants on the deceased.
It alleged that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

sentences.text: Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and he marked documents as Exs.P1 to P22.
She also examined father of the deceased as PW.2, who deposed that the deceased was employed in the company and that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Ex.R1.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending motorcycle.
It also held that the deceased died in the accident due to the injuries suffered.

It considered the age of the deceased at 35 years and his income at Rs.10,000/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards his personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:-

 transportation charges

 Total 19,05,664/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending motorcycle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have filed this appeal.
7. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that Ex.P11 was the salary certificate issued to the deceased by M/s D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers and Exs

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: . P13 and
P14 were returns filed before the ESI Corporation.
He contended that Ex.P14 shows that for 12 days in April, 2019, the deceased was paid a sum of Rs.6,000/- and therefore, the income of the deceased was Rs.15,000 per month.
Hence, he contended that the Tribunal must have considered the income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the insurer, on the other hand, contended that the claimant No.1 herself claimed a sum of Rs.9,000/- per month and therefore, the Tribunal considering NC:
2023:KHC-K:5563 the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month is just and proper.
9.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. The documents on record indicate that the deceased was employed with M/s. D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers.

entities.text: M/s. D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The salary certificate at Ex.P11 issued by PW.2 indicates the salary of the deceased at a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.

This corresponds with the returns filed by M/s. D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers before the Provident Fund Commissioner, which indicate that for 12 days in the month of April, 2019, the deceased was paid a sum of Rs.6,000/-, meaning thereby that his income was a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal must have considered the income at Rs.15,000/- per month.

The deceased was the son of PW.2 who was the Managing Director of M/s. D.D. Engineering Company Contractors and Engineers and therefore, it is quite possible that the deceased was paid a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month as salary.

In view of the above, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-
 Sl.
Particulars

Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Towards loss of dependency 26,88,000/-
 (15,000 + 40% x 12 x 16 x  2/3)
 2 Towards loss of consortium 48,000/-
 3 Towards loss of estate, funeral 36,000/-
 expenses etc.,

4 Towards medical expenses 43,664/-
 Total 28,15,664/-
12.

Since the liability of the insurer is undisputed, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
13. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.19,05,664/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.28,15,664/-, which is payable by the insurer of the offending motorcycle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
14.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC-K:5563 within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
